title: Special Topics: Introduction to Multiphase Flow
description: An introduction to multiphase flows and to the methods used to describe their dynamics. This course covers: (1) the dynamics of particles in fluid from isolated solid particles to suspensions flows,(2) the formation of liquid drops and the generation of sprays, and (3) the dynamics of bubbles.

title: SP: Nanoscale Energy Transport & Conversion
description: A self-contained, application-oriented course covering basic concepts in nanoscale transport and interaction of microscopic energy carriers, mainly electrons, phonons and photons, with an emphasis on new phenomena that emerge at small length and time scales and deviate from macroscopic laws. Topics include (may vary based on time frame): energy levels and statistics of energy carriers; kinetic theory and mean free path; energy transport by waves and the Landauer formalism; near-field radiation; energy transport by particles: Boltzmann transport equation and classical size effect; carrier scattering; energy dissipation. Recent research results and real-world applications are discussed wherever relevant.

title: Biofluid Mechanics
description: Applies the principles of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena to major biological systems, in particular the human body. The course focuses on physiologically relevant flow and transport phenomena from an engineering perspective. Topics covered include blood flow in the cardiovascular system, air flow in the respiratory system, transport processes in joints, and how abnormal fluid mechanics relates to disease. Addresses the rheology of complex fluids, flow through elastic tubes, and transport in porous media. Simple numerical models will be used in the course.
